extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for evaluating patent claims under 35 U.S.C. 112 (indefiniteness, omission of elements/steps, means-plus-function treatment), related claim-drafting defects, duplicate claims, new matter, foreign filing/licensing, disclaimer, and res judicata issues.Provides form paragraphs and examiner notes for making rejections/objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative Term - Term of Degree Rendering Claim Indefinite
rubrics_metrics.description: The term “[1]” in claim [2] is a relative term which renders the claim indefinite. The term “[1]” is not defined by the claim, the specification does not provide a standard for ascertaining the requisite degree, and one of ordinary skill in the art would not be reasonably apprised of the scope of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: In bracket 3, explain which parameter, quantity, or other limitation in the claim has been rendered indefinite by the use of the term appearing in bracket 1. This form paragraph must be preceded by form paragraph 7.34.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broader Range And Narrow Range/Limitation in Same Claim Indefiniteness
rubrics_metrics.description: A broad range or limitation together with a narrow range or limitation that falls within the broad range or limitation (in the same claim) is considered indefinite since the resulting claim does not clearly set forth the metes and bounds of the patent protection desired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains risk where broad language is followed by 'such as' and then narrow language (may be exemplary or required). Cite MPEP § 2173.05(c) and decisions (Ex parte Wu, Steigewald, Hall, Hasche). Examiner Note: insert broader and narrower ranges in brackets; may be modified to fit other instances. Must be preceded by 7.34.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of Antecedent Basis in the Claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] recites the limitation [2] in [3]. There is insufficient antecedent basis for this limitation in the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: In bracket 2, insert the limitation which lacks antecedent basis (e.g., 'said lever' or 'the lever'). In bracket 3, identify where the limitation appears. Use ONLY in aggravated situations where lack of antecedent basis makes scope indeterminate. Must be preceded by 7.34.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Claims (claiming a 'use' without steps) Indefinite / 35 U.S.C. 101 Issue
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] provides for the use of [2], but since the claim does not set forth any steps delimiting how this use is practiced, it is unclear what method/process applicant is intending to encompass. A claim is indefinite where it merely recites a use without any active, positive steps delimiting how this use is practiced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such a recitation can be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 101 as not being a proper process claim. Example cases: Ex parte Dunki; Clinical Products, Ltd. v. Brenner. Examiner Note: 'such as' may render claim indefinite (see MPEP § 2173.05(d)). Must be preceded by 7.34.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modifier of 'Means' Lacks Function (Means-Plus-Function Defect)
rubrics_metrics.description: The word 'means' is preceded by the word(s) '[2]' attempting a 'means' clause to recite an element as a means for performing a specified function; however, since no function is specified by the word(s) preceding 'means,' it is impossible to determine equivalents of the element as required by 35 U.S.C. 112, sixth paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: In bracket 2 insert what is being used (e.g., 'the monoclonal antibodies of claim 4'). See MPEP § 2173.05(q). Must be preceded by 7.34.01. Additional guidance: words before 'means' must convey a function (e.g., 'latch means' is definite; 'conduit means' is indefinite).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims Are a Literal Translation (Narrative/Grammatical Indefiniteness)
rubrics_metrics.description: The claims are generally narrative and indefinite, failing to conform with current U.S. practice. They appear to be a literal translation into English from a foreign document and are replete with grammatical and idiomatic errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this form paragraph when claims are narrative in form and indefinite. Must be preceded by 7.34.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indefinite Claim Language: 'For Example'
rubrics_metrics.description: The phrase 'for example' renders the claim indefinite because it is unclear whether the limitations following the phrase are part of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2173.05(d). Must be preceded by 7.34.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indefinite Claim Language: 'Or The Like'
rubrics_metrics.description: The phrase 'or the like' renders the claim(s) indefinite because the claim(s) include(s) elements not actually disclosed (those encompassed by 'or the like'), thereby rendering the scope of the claim(s) unascertainable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2173.05(d). Must be preceded by 7.34.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indefinite Claim Language: 'Such As'
rubrics_metrics.description: The phrase 'such as' can render the claim indefinite because it is unclear whether the features introduced by such language are merely exemplary or required features of the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rejection must be preceded by form paragraph 7.30.02 or 7.103. (Related to broader/narrow language issues.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential Steps Omitted (35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph - method gaps)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph, as being incomplete for omitting essential steps, such omission amounting to a gap between the steps. The omitted steps are: [2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rejection must be preceded by 7.30.02 or 7.103. In bracket 2, recite the steps omitted and give rationale why omitted steps are critical/essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential Elements Omitted (35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph - structural gaps)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph, as being incomplete for omitting essential elements, such omission amounting to a gap between the elements. The omitted elements are: [2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rejection must be preceded by 7.30.02 or 7.103. In bracket 2, recite omitted elements and rationale for criticality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential Cooperative Relationships Omitted (structural relationships missing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph, as being incomplete for omitting essential structural cooperative relationships of elements, such omission amounting to a gap between the necessary structural connections. The omitted structural cooperative relationships are: [2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rejection must be preceded by 7.30.02 or 7.103. In bracket 2, recite omitted cooperative relationships and rationale for considering them critical or essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection Under 35 U.S.C. 112, Pro Se (narrative claims from pro se applicants)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected as failing to define the invention in the manner required by 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph. The claim(s) are narrative in form and replete with indefinite language; structure must be clearly and positively specified and claims must be in one-sentence form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for pro se filings where claims are disorganized/narrative. Note format of claims in cited patents. Use when pro se deficiencies make scope indefinite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unclear Whether Recited Structure/Material/Acts Preclude Application of 35 U.S.C. 112, Sixth Paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim limitation '[1]' uses 'means for' or 'step for' or a non-structural term coupled with functional language, but is modified by some structure, material, or acts recited in the claim. It is unclear whether the recited structure, material, or acts are sufficient for performing the claimed function because [2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide bracketed explanations: (1) recite limitation in bracket 1, (2) explain why it is unclear whether limitation invokes 112 sixth paragraph. May be used when ambiguous; must be preceded by 7.30.02 and 7.34.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unclear Whether Claim Limitation Invokes 35 U.S.C. 112, Sixth Paragraph When 'Means for' Not Used
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant asserts that claim element '[1]' invokes 112 sixth paragraph, but it is unclear because [2]. Applicant may amend to include 'means for' or 'step for' (properly modified) or present sufficient showing that the claim recites insufficient structure, material, or acts to preclude application of 112 sixth paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: Use in reply situations where applicant argued invocation of sixth paragraph though phrase 'means for' isn't used. Must be preceded by 7.30.02 and 7.34.01. See MPEP § 706.07(a) for final action guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: No Disclosure or Insufficient Disclosure of Corresponding Structure for Means-Plus-Function (112 Sixth Paragraph)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim element '[1]' invokes 35 U.S.C. 112, sixth paragraph. However, the written description fails to disclose the corresponding structure, material, or acts for the claimed function. [2]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant should either (a) amend the specification to expressly recite the corresponding structure/material/acts and link them to the function without introducing new matter, or (b) state on the record what corresponding structure/material/acts (implicitly/inherently set forth) perform the function. In brackets, recite limitation and explain insufficiency. Must be preceded by 7.30.02 and 7.34.01. See 37 CFR 1.75(d) and MPEP §§ 608.01(o), 2181.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fails To Clearly Link or Associate Disclosed Structure to Function (Means-Plus-Function Linkage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim element '[1]' invokes 35 U.S.C. 112, sixth paragraph. However, the written description fails to clearly link or associate the disclosed structure, material, or acts to the claimed function such that one of ordinary skill would recognize what performs the claimed function. [2]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may: (a) amend claim to avoid sixth paragraph interpretation, or (b) amend written description to expressly recite or clearly link corresponding structure/material/acts to function (without new matter), or (c) state on the record where the corresponding structure is set forth in spec. In brackets, recite limitation and explain why linkage is unclear. Must be preceded by 7.30.02 and 7.34.01. See 37 CFR 1.75(d) and MPEP §§ 608.01(o), 2181.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omnibus Claim Rejection (Fails to Particularly Point Out and Distinctly Claim)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph, as being indefinite in that it fails to point out what is included or excluded by the claim language. This claim is an omnibus type claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to reject 'omnibus' type claims (example: 'A device substantially as shown and described.'). Must be preceded by 7.30.02 or 7.103. No further explanation necessary. See MPEP § 1302.04(b) for cancellation by examiner's amendment upon allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark or Trade Name as a Limitation in the Claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] contains the trademark/trade name [2]. Where a trademark or trade name is used in a claim as a limitation to identify or describe a particular material or product, the claim does not comply with 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph because trademark identifies source, not goods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claim scope is uncertain since trademark does not identify/describe the goods. Example: Ex parte Simpson. Examiner Note: insert trademark/trade name and where used in claim in bracket 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification Only Implicitly/Inherently Discloses Structure for Means-Plus-Function (Objected To)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim element '[1]' invokes 112 sixth paragraph. The written description only implicitly or inherently sets forth the corresponding structure/material/acts that perform the claimed function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per 37 CFR 1.75(d) and MPEP §§ 608.01(o), 2181, applicant should: (a) amend claim to avoid sixth paragraph interpretation; or (b) amend spec to expressly recite corresponding structure/material/acts and link them to function (without new matter); or (c) state on the record what corresponding structure/material/acts (implicitly/inherently set forth) perform the function. In bracket 1 recite limitation invoking sixth paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim Limitation Interpreted under 35 U.S.C. 112, Sixth Paragraph (identify corresponding structure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim limitation '[1]' has been interpreted under 35 U.S.C. 112, sixth paragraph, because it uses a non-structural term '[2]' coupled with functional language '[3]' without reciting sufficient structure. The non-structural term is not preceded by a structural modifier. [4]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since limitation invokes sixth paragraph, claim is interpreted to cover the corresponding structure described in the specification that achieves the claimed function, and equivalents. Examiner must identify corresponding structure in spec (bracket 6) and provide references. Applicant may amend or present argument. Provide bracketed items: limitation, non-structural term, functional language, explanation why non-structural, claim numbers containing limitation, corresponding structure references. See Supplementary Examination Guidelines (76 FR 7162).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate Claims — Warning (Substantial Duplicate)
rubrics_metrics.description: When two claims are duplicates, or are so close that they both cover the same thing despite slight differences, the Office may object to the duplicate claim as a substantial duplicate of an allowed claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 7.05.05: Applicant is advised that if claim [1] is allowable, claim [2] will be objected to under 37 CFR 1.75 as a substantial duplicate. Use when duplicate claims are present but not allowable to give applicant opportunity to correct. See MPEP § 706.03(k).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate Claims — Objection (37 CFR 1.75)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] objected under 37 CFR 1.75 as being a substantial duplicate of claim [2]. When claims are duplicates or too close in content, it is proper after allowing one claim to object to the other as a substantial duplicate of the allowed claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If duplicate claims are not allowable, use form paragraph 7.05.05 (warning) instead. See MPEP § 706.03(k).

rubrics_metrics.name: Objection to New Matter Added to Specification (35 U.S.C. 132(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The amendment filed [1] is objected to under 35 U.S.C. 132(a) because it introduces new matter into the disclosure. The added material not supported by the original disclosure is: [2]. Applicant is required to cancel the new matter in the reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: Not to be used in reissue applications (use 14.22.01). In bracket 2 identify new matter by page/line/drawing figures and provide explanation addressing applicant's support and unresolved questions. If new matter is added to claims, also make a rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph (form paragraph 7.31.01). See MPEP § 2163 and §§ 608.04.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign Filing Without License — Abandonment and Bar (35 U.S.C. 182–185)
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing or disclosing the invention in a foreign country in violation of an order (section 181) or without obtaining the required license may result in abandonment of the invention and bar to patent under 35 U.S.C. 182–185. A patent may be invalid if foreign filing occurred without license unless through error and without deceptive intent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If examiner learns of a corresponding foreign application filed before six months after U.S. filing and the invention was made in the U.S., refer application to Licensing and Review Section. Pending investigation, application may be returned to TC. Licensing/Review will request transfer if action under 35 U.S.C. 185 necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclaimer — Claim Subject Matter Disclaimed by Applicant's Acts
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims may be rejected on the ground that applicant has disclaimed the subject matter involved, e.g., by failure to present claims for interference, failure to copy a claim when suggested by examiner, or failure to respond/appeal within time to an examiner's rejection of copied claims for interference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rejection on disclaimer applies to all claims not patentably distinct from the disclaimed subject matter as well as directly involved claims. Use form paragraphs 7.48 and 7.49 for disclaimer-based rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Res Judicata — Rejection Based on Earlier Adjudication
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. [2] based upon claim [3] of Patent No. [4]. Failure to present claims or take necessary interference steps after notification constitutes a disclaimer and res judicata may be proper ground for rejection when earlier decision was by Board or reviewing court and no further review opportunity exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only when earlier decision was a Board or court decision and no opportunity for further review exists. When making res judicata rejections, also ordinarily act on basis of prior art. See cited cases (In re Oguie, In re Freeman, Edgerton v. Kingland). Examiner Note: Use form paragraph only after applicant notified that interference proceedings must be instituted and applicant refused to copy claims. Insert statutory basis (102(g) etc.) and patent number and other references in brackets.
